claim: uoi registers a manager history invalidation listener. Its callback acts only when notification hostId matches manager.getHostId() and scope.get(N3,hostId) is that same manager; it increments q3 except item-content-only entity-key invalidation, calls Toi, and calls Poi only when removed is truthy. This identity guard limits stale-manager callbacks at source level.

The complete X3 constructor only assigns the supplied scope to this.scope. It contains no manager construction or registration. The inherited mRs useState initializer constructs Cee(scope), whose import binds to shared X3, so creation of that registry wrapper is distinct from manager creation.

X3.registerHost returns before loi if BI already includes the supplied hostId. Combining this guard with the BI default callback exposes a local-key early-return possibility; it does not prove the default BI or N3 callback has run.

For a hostId absent from BI, registerHost first appends it to BI, then calls loi(scope,hostId), and calls addManager only for a non-null result. A null creation result can leave a registered host key without a manager in this source path.

refreshRendererManager does nothing unless getImplForHostId(hostId) is non-null. Otherwise its expression invokes deleteManager then registerHost; it does not itself preserve the old manager or directly instantiate a replacement.

addManager reads the supplied object getHostId() and the currently registered manager. Only a distinct non-null prior manager is passed to mDr and Dfn.dispose; only when prior !== supplied does it call uoi for the supplied object. Arbitrary supplied managers remain accepted, so this is not exclusive Dfn identity proof.
conditions: prior != null && prior !== supplied for disposal

claim: addManager deduplicates hostId in BI, clears CF(hostId), calls gai, stores the supplied object into N3(hostId), then increments lli. These are source writes and calls; actual reducer/atom persistence and callback delivery are not established.

addManager resets queryClient queries for [...f6,hostId] only when there is a distinct non-null prior manager, hostId is literal `local`, and e6?.daybreakPreferences is non-null. The capability condition does not establish ChatGPT mode or an executed reset.

deleteManager disposes a non-null currently registered object via mDr/Dfn.dispose, removes the hostId from BI, sets N3(hostId)=null, calls boi with disconnected/error:null/registry_delete_manager, and increments lli. Disposal effects beyond these call boundaries are inherited/unknown.

addRegistryCallback returns scope.watch(...) and its callback reads lli, suppresses its first own e() invocation with a local boolean, then calls the supplied callback on later watch invocations. Actual watch scheduling/subscription disposal behavior is a dependency boundary.

waitForManagerForHostId immediately returns Promise.resolve(existing) if found; otherwise it reuses a scope-local fli Map promise per hostId, installs a registry callback, and when a manager appears calls the returned unsubscribe, deletes the pending map entry and resolves. This complete method has no explicit rejection or timeout path; callback delivery/liveness remain unverified.

getForHostId and getImplForHostId return N3(hostId) only when BI includes that hostId; otherwise they return null. The methods share registry gating but are not evidence of an actual existing manager.

getDefault returns scope.get(zoi); the zoi callback reads N3(II) and throws Missing default AppServerManager when null. getForHostIdOrThrowWhenDefaultHost throws for a missing literal local manager while returning null for a missing other host.

bli destructures the supplied scope and hostId, creates a new X3(scope) wrapper, then calls getForHostId(hostId) and reads existing conversation/turn/stream state. This is a lookup in its complete dynamic-tool caller, not manager creation or registerHost/addManager publication.

Sli returns false for callerSource literal chatgpt; its await Eli(request) branch looks up new X3(scope).getImplForHostId(hostId) and checks conversation plus non-follower stream role. Its other branch uses KI and getConversation/readThread under disposal guards, returning false on outer failure. These branch literals do not establish the mode of ordinary composer or current runtime.
conditions: await Eli(request) selects manager lookup vs KI branch

claim: Cli constructs an item/tool/call request. When await Eli(request) is true it looks up an existing manager with new X3(scope).getImplForHostId(hostId), calls onRequest only when non-null and reports that source dispatch. Otherwise it stores an AbortController in Z3, awaits bli with transport mcp, and deletes only its still-current controller in finally. This is tool dispatch/cleanup, not manager registration.

The frozen ERs caller receives mRs() and contains durable/remote registration and renderer-refresh effects. Its source explicitly excludes the current hostId and local: prefixed removed hosts from deletion. Its durable/remote conditions are retained from the earlier contract; this caller is not promoted into an observed ordinary-local registration event.

The local default-key factory, an X3 wrapper over a scope, and explicit manager replacement are separate implementation responsibilities. A maintainable implementation can model their interfaces separately while requiring behavior receipts to settle actual initialization/cancellation/disposal ownership. This is a design inference, not source proof of runtime architecture.

Actual ordinary UI host/scope identity, evaluation order, atom mounting, hostRegistry-provided manager identity, installed manager identity and completion/disposal/cancellation effects remain unresolved. Decisive next evidence is an authorized source-qualified behavior receipt linking the local N3 evaluation/register/replace branch to the same mounted composer scope and manager, with restart/cancel/error outcomes.
